overall_reason: A detector test fixture whose visible design is entirely framework default: gray-50 page, white shadow-sm cards with rounded corners and coloured side or top accent strips, Inter throughout and tracked-caps section labels; the specimens are deliberate, but the look around them is a default nobody chose, and as a design artifact it reads as a model's stock card kit.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: 16 white cards, each radius 4-12px with shadow rgba(0,0,0,.1) 0 1px 3px and a 2-8px accent strip on one edge, on #f9fafb, in Inter with #6b7280/#9ca3af secondary text. Beyond the sweep's saas-card-kit cluster, the screenshots add the accent-strip card (side and top/bottom) as the unit of every section, which is the stock 'callout card' of generated dashboards.
findings.before: Every item is a rounded white card with a coloured edge strip
findings.after: For a specimen sheet, show each case as a plain row (name in mono, one-line note) with the specimen beside it at reduced size, so the page's own chrome does not repeat the tell it documents
findings.why: The chrome and the specimens share one recipe, so nothing on the page reads as chosen.

findings.where: accent strips across all four sections
findings.evidence: Seven unrelated accent hues on one page with no meaning attached: blue, purple, red (Tailwind side-tab), blue, violet, green, red (CSS side-tab), blue, purple, emerald (top/bottom), cyan, violet, pink (dark mode). T-DELETION: recolouring them all one hue loses no information.
findings.before: border-blue-500 / border-purple-500 / border-red-500 / border-emerald-500 / border-cyan-400 / pink
findings.after: One accent token, or none; if variety is needed for detector coverage, vary the property (width, side, shorthand) and keep the hue constant
findings.why: A rotating rainbow of accents is decoration standing in for a decision; a reader looks for a code in the colours and finds none.

findings.where: section heads "TAILWIND SIDE-TAB", "CSS SIDE-TAB", "TOP/BOTTOM + ROUNDED", "DARK MODE"
findings.evidence: Failed T-LABEL-TRANSFORM: the h2s are 14px uppercase, tracked and grey, the same size as the h3 card titles (sweep flat_hierarchy: h2 14px = h3 14px). Set in sentence case they read as well or better, so the caps are costume and the only thing separating sections from cards.
findings.after: h2 at 20-24px sentence case, untracked, body colour: "Tailwind side-tab"
findings.why: Tracked small caps as the only section marker is a generated-page habit and flattens the hierarchy to two levels.

findings.where: every section at 1440, right two thirds
findings.evidence: Cards are capped at 448px wide and left-aligned while section rules run the full 1376px; about 65% of each section's container is empty at 1440 (tiles 0-1).
findings.after: Grid the specimens: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(320px, 1fr)) so each section fills its rule, or cap the whole page at ~720px so the rules match the cards
findings.why: Full-width rules over a narrow column leave a dead right-hand field and make the page look unfinished.

strengths: Every card names exactly the property it exhibits ("border-e-8 + rounded-l", "border-left-width: 3px") with a one-line note; for a fixture, the copy is precise and complete.
The intro line states the page's purpose plainly: "Every example on this page should be detected by the anti-pattern scanner."
not_investigated: Purpose: this is a scanner fixture, not a client page, so T-RIVAL-NAME, T-MIRROR, T-THREE-LINE and T-STOCK-ORDER have no client or category to test against; recorded as run, no finding.
Tailwind was shimmed with @tailwindcss/browser@4; small differences from the original v3 render are possible.
